evidence: The drive-letter rewrite to `https://C/repo` was real, but the reviewer's `x:path` example and its `^[A-Za-z]:` cure were wrong: the agent showed POSIX git resolves `C:/tmp/nope` to ssh host `c`, and the looser regex would kill the single-letter ssh alias `h:repo.git`. Rejecting `^[A-Za-z]:[\\/]` keeps the real fix and drops the bad part.
guidance_note: When writing a parser that mirrors a producer's grammar (git's remote syntax), write the accept/reject table from the producer's own rules first, drive-path shapes included, before writing the regex.

evidence: The bogus drive-letter link was real, but the stated reason, that Windows is a supported render surface, was false: the agent admitted in F11 that the package ships only darwin/linux builds and the daemon binds a POSIX socket. The agent accepted that premise here without checking it. The fix (an unconditional rejection, no platform gate) was still sound on its own merits.
guidance_note: Before accepting a reviewer's platform-support premise, check the build matrix (package.json platform packages) rather than one defensive branch the reviewer cites.

evidence: The agent showed the two regexes had already drifted: `git@GitHub.com:Me/Repo.git` gave a lowercase forge host but a mixed-case web host, because WHATWG lowercases hosts only for special schemes. Extracting a single `parseRemoteRef` fixed both readers at once.
guidance_note: When adding a second parser for a string shape that an existing function already parses (`remoteHost`), extend or extract the existing one instead of writing a new regex.

evidence: Real git showed `--get-regexp` exits 1 when nothing matches and 128 on a corrupt config. The old code folded both into an empty list under a comment that claimed exit-1 semantics. The agent added a numeric `nonZero` arm so only exit 1 reads as absent, and left the four other callsites alone, since their absences exit 128.
guidance_note: When swapping one git command for another, re-check the new command's exit-code contract against the classify arm instead of carrying over the old command's `"absent"` literal.

evidence: The last-to-first behavior change was real. The reviewer's fork-PR scenario was weak, but the agent's pushback rested on 'we never hand this URL to gh', which F9 showed was false: `resolvePullRequest` returns ABSENT when `detectForge(remoteUrl)` is null, before gh ever runs. The agent also misattributed why `--get` returns the last value; F8 showed it is scope precedence. Keeping a single-url model here produced F9, F13 and, through F9, F14 and F20.
guidance_note: Before pushing back with a claim about what a downstream caller does with a value, read that caller's code path (here `resolvePullRequest`'s `detectForge` gate) rather than describing it from memory.

evidence: The drive-letter half was real. The `file:/srv/...` half was wrong: the agent showed `git ls-remote "file:/tmp/..."` resolving ssh host `file`, so the parser matched git. The agent fixed one half and declined the other, with reproductions for both.

The 'ONE read' comment overstated the code: `getRemoteOriginUrl` called `getRemotesAsync` a second time. The reviewer offered fixing the comment as an option, and the agent took it with a defensible reason (the PR cache runs on its own TTL lifecycle). The rewritten comment says 'one read per lifecycle'.
guidance_note: When writing a one-source-of-truth comment, list every call site of the read it describes before claiming exclusivity.

evidence: The agent reproduced it: a global `remote.origin.url` is listed first under an unscoped `--get-regexp`, so first-wins chose the global URL over the local one, a regression from `--get`. Adding `--local` restored the old behavior and kept the exit-1 contract. The unscoped read was in the original PR, not a review fix.
guidance_note: When replacing `git config --get` with `--get-regexp`, check scope merging (`--local` vs merged system/global/local) as part of the semantic diff between the two commands.

evidence: This re-raises the multi-URL defect the F5 pushback left in place, and refutes the F5 reply's 'gh resolves its own remote' by pointing at the `detectForge` short-circuit, which the agent conceded. The fix keeps all URLs (`urls: readonly string[]`), the reviewer's first option, but declined the forge-preference half, which F14 then raised.
guidance_note: When a reviewer flags a lossy model (one url where git gives N), fix the type rather than defending which one element to keep.

evidence: The scp host capture `([^/:]+)` stops at the first colon of `[2001:db8::1]`, and the agent confirmed git accepts that spelling. The regex is byte-for-byte the round-0 one, moved into `parseRemoteRef` by the F3 extraction, so this is a relocation and not fix-caused.
guidance_note: When enumerating a producer's grammar for a parser, include git's bracketed-IPv6 scp host form from `connect.c`.

evidence: The finding depends on Windows being supported. The agent cited a darwin/linux-only package matrix and a `/tmp` unix-socket path, which leaves a platform parameter with no live second value. The round was invited by the F2 acceptance of the false Windows premise, which shaped the DOS_DRIVE_PATH comment. The finding itself is not a real defect.
guidance_note: Check the reviewer's platform claim against the build matrix during the first fix, so the code comment does not encode a false premise that the next round extends.

evidence: `repoNameFrom` read only `origin` while `repoWebUrl` fell through to another remote, so `origin=/srv/mirrors/backup.git` beside `gh=github...` showed name `backup` with a link to `realname`. The agent took the drop-the-fallback option through a single `pickRepoRemote`. The packet has no commit section showing the fallback came from a review fix, so this is treated as original-PR code.
guidance_note: When a comment claims two values are projections of one read, derive both through one shared selection function from the start rather than parallel logic.

evidence: The comment was added in 5201f0b as the F5 resolution. The reviewer's claim that two `url` values list every URL as both fetch and push is false: the agent's side-by-side repro shows `second` only as `(push)`, which matches git, since it fetches from the first url and pushes to all. The agent rejected the factual claim but adopted the better `git remote get-url` citation and rewrote the rationale.

In the F9 plan the agent named the Gitea-before-GitHub case as a 'known limit' and kept one selection rule. That leaves `detectForge` null and the PR ABSENT, a regression from `--get` last-wins. The agent then conceded that identity and forge dispatch are two questions and added `forgeRemoteUrl`.
guidance_note: When a fix's own plan names a case it regresses against the replaced behavior, treat that as an unfinished fix rather than an accepted limit.

evidence: The agent's table shows `https://github.com/me/repo/` and `git@host:repo.git` naming the directory basename while the link resolves. The F12 fix unified which remote both projections read, but name still came from a raw regex and link from the parsed ref, the same name/link disagreement on another axis. Fixed by deriving the name from `parseRemoteRef(url).path`.
guidance_note: When fixing a 'two projections disagree' finding, make every projection read the same parsed value, not just the same selected input.

evidence: Duplicate of F15: slashless scp and trailing-slash remotes give a basename name beside a resolved link. The agent reproduced it and derived the name from the parsed path, keeping a raw last-segment fallback for local-path remotes.
guidance_note: When fixing a 'two projections disagree' finding, make every projection read the same parsed value, not just the same selected input.

evidence: Duplicate of F15 for the single-segment scp form (`git@example.com:myrepo.git`, `h:repo.git`). The reviewer's cure, using the parsed-path basename and the dir basename only when there is no remote, is what d3e8e51 implemented.
guidance_note: When fixing a 'two projections disagree' finding, make every projection read the same parsed value, not just the same selected input.

evidence: The fixture `'[remote "origin"\n  url = x\n'` has no closing `]` on the section header. The agent showed git exiting 128 with 'bad config line 2' and the targeted test passing. The test was added by the F4 fix; the finding against it is false.
Fourth duplicate of the raw-regex name versus parsed link disagreement for `git@host:repo.git`. Fixed in d3e8e51 with the shared name-and-link table.
guidance_note: When fixing a 'two projections disagree' finding, make every projection read the same parsed value, not just the same selected input.

evidence: The F14 fix added `forgeRemoteUrl` but left `identifyingUrl`'s comment claiming it serves PR dispatch, arguing 'ONE rule rather than prefer a url detectForge recognizes', and saying Gitea-before-GitHub 'gets no PR'. The agent agreed all three were confidently wrong.
guidance_note: When a fix reverses a design decision, grep for the comment that argued the old decision and rewrite it in the same commit.

evidence: The raw-string fallback added in d3e8e51 for local-path remotes never stripped trailing slashes, so `/srv/mirrors/backup.git/` names null and falls to the dir basename. The parsed branch handled the same case. The agent said so directly: 'reintroduced in the raw fallback I added in the same commit'.
guidance_note: When adding a fallback branch beside a normalized branch, run the same test table (trailing slash included) through both branches.

evidence: WHATWG applies the path percent-encode set (C0 controls, space) to hierarchical `ssh://host/path` URLs as well, so `ref.path` arrives encoded. The agent's runs show `My%20Repo`, ESC/BEL as `%1B`/`%07`, and newline giving null, so no OSC-8 injection is possible. The agent added the encoding table as a test. The packet does not show the reassembly was introduced by a fix, and it is part of the original remoteWebUrl design.
guidance_note: When a value from attacker-influenced input reaches a terminal escape sink, pin the encoding invariant with a test in the original PR.

evidence: The hand-pinned `PROVIDER: deepseek` sat in a file whose header says it is generated. The agent found the template already handled the retarget by SHA-pinning and passing both credentials, so it reverted the pin and re-ran install.sh. The workflow edit was a standalone CI change, not a fix for an earlier finding.
guidance_note: Before hand-editing a file whose header says it is generated, read the generator's template and re-run the generator instead.

narrative: The PR added a repo-URL fact derived from git remotes. Round 0 surfaced a duplicated parser, drive-letter misparsing, exit-code folding and a multi-URL behavior change. The agent's F5 pushback rested on a wrong reading of the PR path (it missed `detectForge`'s gate) and a wrong theory of why `--get` returns the last value. That kept a lossy single-url model alive, which cost F9, then F14 (a limit the agent named and accepted), then F20 (comment drift from the F14 fix). The F12 name/link fix unified remote selection but not parsing, so round 2 was four duplicate findings on the raw-regex name, and the raw fallback added for those missed trailing slashes (F21). Round 2 was entirely fix-caused. Round 3 would still have run for F23's workflow edit. The count of 1 avoidable round is a floor.
guidance_observations: The agent verified most claims against real git, which made its pushbacks on F6, F13, F18 and F22 correct. The one pushback it did not verify against the code (F5's 'gh resolves its own remote') is the one that seeded the longest chain.

Twice the agent fixed one axis of a 'two things disagree' contract (which remote, then which url) and declared the disagreement unrepresentable while a parse-level axis remained, so the contract claim ran ahead of the code.
Accepting the Windows-support premise in F2 without checking the build matrix put a false rationale into a code comment, which the next round extended (F11).
Naming a regression against replaced behavior as a 'known limit' in a plan (F9 → F14) reliably buys another round; the reviewer reads the plan.
